blocks.h2: A Yearly Plumbing Checklist for Evanston Homes
blocks.body: Each year, flush the water heater and test its relief valve. Test the sump pump before spring. Check the sewer line if you've had root problems. Look under sinks for slow drips and stiff shutoff valves. In fall, drain outdoor faucets. Every few years, have a plumber look at the gas connections and the condition of your supply pipe. A maintenance visit covers all of this in one trip.

blocks.h2: What We Look for in an Older Evanston Home
blocks.body: In a house built before 1940, we pay special attention to a few things: the type and condition of the supply pipe, how the sewer lateral is holding up, whether the water heater vents properly through an old chimney and whether old shutoff valves still work. We also look for abandoned gas branches and outdated connectors. You get a plain-language summary and prices for anything we recommend.

You get a plain summary of each system: fine, worth watching or needs attention. We note ages, like when the water heater was made, and conditions, like stiff shutoffs or signs of sewer trouble. Any recommended work comes with a flat price. You decide what to do and when.
